what: Smoke test of the Phase 2 train.py argv on a two-language mini corpus (afr + deu, 500 lines each, copied from wili_corpus_shared) with the patched fp64 spm_train. One run per candidate base tokenizer, each with the exact flags its SLURM script would use.
finding: The LLM-tokenizer-to-UNILID-base path (train.py:52 _convert_to_unigram_base, reached from train.py:458-462) is solved for BYTE-LEVEL BPE tokenizers only. It preserves the source's pretokenizer, so a SentencePiece-style source yields a byte_level=False base (language_specific_trainer.py:263 warns and overrides --byte-level), and the per-language SentencePiece path then refuses vocabulary entries containing a raw carriage return. Mistral-7B-v0.2 and Llama-2-7b-hf are blocked by this; Mistral-Nemo and Llama-3.2-1B are not. Unblocking needs an author decision (byte-level re-encoding of the source vocabulary, dropping the offending entries, or a different --per-lang-counts-method); each yields a different model, so none was chosen here.
also_measured: Phase 3's from-scratch argv (--no-reuse-base, no --base-tokenizer-path) runs: at --vocab-size 4000 on the mini corpus it trained a base in 14.47 s, wrote it to <results-dir>/tokenizers/langspec_base_tokenizer.json with exactly 4000 Unigram entries, and its first four tokens are <s> </s> <pad> <unk> followed by 'G-dot', the same convention as the published wili_100k_500 base, so a divergence in the Phase 3 gating check would be a genuine vocabulary difference rather than an ordering artifact.
